"Instead of burning or shredding garden prunings from winter cleanup, consider transforming them into a dead hedge. This eco-friendly alternative serves as an effective windbreak, provides shelter for wildlife, and helps demarcate spaces within your garden. To build one, drive stakes or old fence posts into the ground in two parallel rows spaced 50cm apart, then weave pruned material between them, placing thicker branches at the base for stability. Over time, the structure will settle and compact. For a festive touch to your winter gardening plans, pre-order Paul Smith’s *The Book Of Seeds* (Ivy Press, £30), launching in February. This lavishly illustrated guide, authored by the former director of Kew’s Millennium Seed Bank, showcases 600 captivating seed species, including the oddly Trump-haired ‘black seed’ and minuscule orchid seeds. Meanwhile, to brighten winter gardens, plant winter-flowering clematis. Varieties like *Clematis cirrhosa* ‘Advent Bells’ (3m x 1.5m) and *C. cirrhosa* var. *balearica* (2.5m x 1.5m) offer fragrant, cream-colored blooms with maroon markings, while ‘Jingle Bells’ (5m x 2m) produces pristine white flowers. These resilient climbers thrive in sunny, sheltered spots, blooming from December to February. Is there anything else I can help with?"
